name: NJ-04
label: Likely R

key_factors: Republican-leaning district (R+14) held by long-serving incumbent Chris Smith
Challenger Rachel Peace badly outspent, with about $5,000 on hand versus Smith's $488,000
Prediction markets price a Democratic win at only about 3%
No public general-election polling; structural fundamentals dominate
model.rationale: Smith combines a strongly Republican district, decades of incumbency, and a lopsided financial advantage, while Peace has raised little and drawn no outside investment; prediction markets corroborate an overwhelming Republican edge.
model.watch: A late surge of outside spending against Smith or an unforeseen scandal could narrow the race, but no current evidence points that way.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Chris Smith, one of the House's longest-serving members, seeks another term in a New Jersey district that leans Republican by roughly fourteen points at the presidential level. He enters the fall with about $488,000 on hand after raising nearly $600,000, while Democrat Rachel Peace has raised about $34,000 and reports just over $5,000 in cash. No outside groups have invested meaningfully in the race, and no public general-election polling is available.

Prediction markets give Peace roughly a three percent chance of winning. Even if the national environment tilts toward Democrats, the combination of district partisanship, Smith's entrenched incumbency, and the wide financial gap leaves little apparent path to an upset. The race is rated Safe Republican, with the main uncertainty lying in turnout in a low-information contest rather than any sign of competitive vulnerability.
